01 / The company brain

Keep the knowledge
behind the work.

A task list leaves some important questions open. What do the goals mean? Why was a decision taken, and what evidence supports the account of what happened? The project needs those answers too.

The Lab gives that knowledge a continuing structure. Definitions state the important meanings. Connected records let the next reader inspect attempts, claim support and decisions governing change.

When the work changes hands, those connections give the next participant a place to begin.

CyberAlchemy Lab / Getting started

Start here

Begin with the ideas behind knowledge and work in the Lab, then follow the parts you need in more detail.

5 minute read · No prior knowledge of the Lab required

Organize knowledge and work

CyberAlchemy organizes knowledge and work. It connects meaning, purpose, performed work and possible next changes. A returning person or agent has records to examine instead of reconstructing everything from conversations.

Consider an incomplete export report. We need a meaning for “complete,” permission for relevant data, an inspectable comparison and a response decision. The Lab gives each responsibility a place in the same project knowledge.

The guide follows the fictional Northstar incident. This page introduces the concepts used in that investigation.

Organize knowledge and work

CyberAlchemy organizes knowledge and work. It connects meaning, purpose, performed work and possible next changes. A returning person or agent has records to examine instead of reconstructing everything from conversations.

The guide follows the fictional Northstar incident. This page introduces the concepts used in that investigation.

Begin with what the words mean

A definition states meaning and boundaries. An accepted exact version is a basic unit of authority over meaning within an accountable owner’s declared purpose and scope.

For this export, completeness requires every selected identifier from the declared account, filters and fixed snapshot in the saved output. That examines identifier coverage. Value accuracy and data-access permission need their own requirements.

Common mistake

Formal definition, source explanation and boundaries

The formal statement governs the meaning. The short introduction above helps you read it; it does not replace its requirements.

Source explanatory wording

The project-owned record that says exactly what a term means, where that meaning applies, and how drift can be challenged. A passing candidate is not canonical until its owner admits it.

Exact governing statement

A Definition is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic artifact that assigns a term one normative meaning within an exact authority scope. It is structurally complete only when stable identity, applicability, exclusions, a scientific/formal normative voice, explicitly non-normative plain-language and domain-context voices, boundaries, admitted source posture, primary consumers, a synchronized registry postimage, generated index, and a current drift route are declared. Only an exact owner promotion decision can make one exact Definition version

Compiling software
from explicit models

We’re building Craft as a software-design, domain-modeling and enforceable-architecture product for a closed beta. The aim is to compile software from an explicit model, keeping its meaning connected to the choices that shape the code.

Craft sits within CyberAlchemy Lab’s wider model of knowledge and work. The Lab guide follows a requirement into a project, assigned work and evidence for an owner decision. Here we follow the software model and implementation developed during that work. Craft’s design contracts and the Lab’s acceptance and deployment decisions retain their own responsibilities.
